result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A uses a line chart with direct end labels and a '$ thousands' axis title. It makes West stand out with a thicker, saturated blue line against muted grays, so the colors stay restrained and you can tell the lines apart without relying on hue. B also has a clear headline, KPI cards and direct labels, but its three hue-only lines all have the same weight, it repeats a legend that isn't needed, its y-axis has no unit label, and West gets no visual emphasis inside the chart itself. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers use line charts with direct end labels and headlines saying West grew fastest. B makes West stand out in the chart itself with a thick blue line against muted grays, labels the axis '$ thousands', and adds a data table. A gives all three lines equal weight, tells them apart only by hue, keeps a redundant legend, and has no unit label on the axis itself; its unit appears only in the subtitle and footnote.
